title: CRASH-073: parseurl scheme colon slash just path length not decremented oob read (out-of-bounds-read)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow at Zend/zend_alloc.c:403 in _estrndup when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 6fcc1515cba0d4719bf1edd831d242db9bc72f0f, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/url.c:143 (defect) / ext/standard/url.c:292 (faulting estrndup)
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has _estrndup at Zend/zend_alloc.c:403 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #1, under the libc leaf memcpy at frame #0, which is not declared: a fault there can be tied to this case only through its caller, and the launcher reports no return address); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the nested layer present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the stock arm ran this case to its normal end, the corpus's pristine record says it completes, and revocation-sanity completed on this arm) and completed with no fault; native PHP: OK; nodes allocated 3716, table capacity 262144 (cumulative, not a high-water: reported, not gated)

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the nested allocator layer retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: reached (the stock arm ran this case to its normal end, the corpus's pristine record says it completes, and revocation-sanity completed on this arm) and completed with no fault; native PHP: OK; nodes allocated 4030, table capacity 262144 (cumulative, not a high-water: reported, not gated)

virtual-nested-exact.oracle: virtual-nested-pools with each payload bounded to the caller's request instead of REAL_SIZE(n): the arm that can see a defect inside PHP's own rounding slack (php-real-exact)
virtual-nested-exact.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3f8f401c74 in memcpy; the fault is in memcpy (?:0), outside PHP's tree; its frame chain passes PHP's allocator (_estrndup@zend_alloc.c:437) before any declared site, through which no access can be attributed (above nothing): the fault may be the port's, whatever lies deeper

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the same trigger on stock CheriBSD purecap -- no nested layer at all, the real interpreter cross-built by ports/php/cheribsd/build.sh -- in the boot at the platform default (security.cheri.runtime_revocation_default=1, every_free=0): a SIGPROT at the ASan site with the bounds-malloc control faulting in the same boot, the same binary run with revocation off as the pair that attributes the fault, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json cheribsd-default)

status: built 2026-10-27 from the corpus and our native oracle; what has run is in this record's arms (verdict, verdict_from) and under results/
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK. That is the selection, by measurement; which mechanism hides it, and which arm sees it, is what the arms record. Collected by the corpus as fuzz (historical-known, confidence high).
